title: Good and bad trades
line: When giving a piece for a piece leaves you ahead.

steps.text: A trade is a capture answered by a capture. Count the points: what you take, minus what you lose.
The rook on d5 is guarded by a pawn. Capture it with the knight anyway, and count.
steps.after: You gave a knight, worth 3, for a rook, worth 5. You are 2 points ahead.

steps.text: Now a bad trade to avoid: the pawn on e5 is guarded by the pawn on d6.
Your queen can capture the pawn on e5 or the knight on b5. Capture the one nothing guards.

wrong.e2e5: Then the pawn on d6 captures your queen: you take 1 and lose 9.

steps.after: The knight was worth 3, and nothing could capture back.

steps.text: A bishop for a knight, or a rook for a rook, is an even trade: the points stay level.

summary: A trade helps you when what you capture is worth more than what you lose. Count before you capture.
